boundary: Pass 6024 reformulates alpha(W(2n-1,q)) as a matrix-rank extremal problem and VERIFIES the reformulation on the actual optima at q=2 and q=3. It does NOT solve the odd-q case. The reformulation is elementary and, like everything else in this thread with a short proof, presumed classical

pass_6024_the_unification.so: the rank bound is identical at every q. What differs is how much freedom the entries have, and that is the entire reason the even-q answer is a clean formula while the odd-q answers resist one
pass_6024_the_unification.statement: alpha(W(2n-1,q)) = the maximum k for which some k x k ANTISYMMETRIC matrix over F_q, with zero diagonal and ALL off-diagonal entries nonzero, has rank at most 2n
pass_6024_the_unification.the_mechanism: at q=2 there is exactly ONE nonzero field element, so the Gram matrix is FORCED to be J_k - I_k and the parity of its rank caps k at 2n+1. At odd q there are q-1 nonzero values, the matrix is not forced, and k can exceed 2n+1 -- 7 at q=3 and 18 at q=5 against 2n+1 = 5
pass_6024_the_unification.why: a set of pairwise non-collinear points is a set of vectors whose Gram matrix under the symplectic form has zero diagonal and nonzero off-diagonal entries; the vectors span a subspace of F_q^(2n), so the Gram rank is at most 2n

pass_6025_the_simplex_connection.observation: k vectors pairwise non-orthogonal with all Gram entries EQUAL is the symplectic analogue of a regular simplex
pass_6025_the_simplex_connection.status: an interpretation connecting two known mechanisms, not a new theorem
pass_6025_the_simplex_connection.the_reading: at q=2 the optimum is FORCED into simplex shape because there is only one nonzero value to be constant at; at odd q it is not forced, and that is why 7 and 18 fit no formula
pass_6025_the_simplex_connection.the_repo_owns_this_mechanism: Pass 1614's Hoffman-tight criterion: a coclique meets the ratio bound iff its characteristic vectors form a regular simplex at constant inner product

pass_6026_the_odd_q_question_restated.new_form: what is the maximum k for a rank-at-most-4 antisymmetric F_q matrix with all off-diagonal entries nonzero?
pass_6026_the_odd_q_question_restated.old_form: what is alpha(W(3,q)) for odd q? -- 7, 18, and then unknown
pass_6026_the_odd_q_question_restated.still_open: q=9 at 2n=4, where the best construction is 51 against a bound of 80
pass_6026_the_odd_q_question_restated.why_this_is_better: it is a pure matrix problem with no geometry in it, it makes the q-dependence explicit as the number of available nonzero values, and it explains why q=2 is the only clean case
